maker.title: Free Sprite Sheet Maker
maker.intro: Turn individual images or an animated GIF into a clean, organized sprite sheet. This free online sprite sheet maker aligns your frames, lets you check the animation, and exports PNG with optional JSON metadata — no account needed.
maker.stepsTitle: How to make a sprite sheet in three steps

steps.title: 1. Add your images or GIF
steps.text: Drop PNG, JPG, or static WebP frames into Images mode, or switch to GIF to extract an animation. Image filenames sort naturally, so run-2 comes before run-10. If you still need artwork, generate assets on the home page, then come back here to arrange the frames.

steps.title: 2. Arrange and check every frame
steps.text: Choose a grid, horizontal strip, or vertical strip. Set columns, outer margin, and frame gaps, then pick an alignment for different-sized images. Use the animation preview to find missing or misplaced frames. Drag the frame handles to fix their order before you export.

steps.title: 3. Download a useful asset
steps.text: Download a transparent sprite sheet as PNG, add JSON, CSS, XML, or an animated GIF to a ZIP, or open the result directly in Sprite Sheet Cutter. That handoff carries the grid settings, names, and timing within this browser tab.

maker.featuresTitle: A sprite sheet generator built around your frame sequence

features.title: GIF to sprite sheet, with complete frames
features.text: A GIF can store only the pixels that change between frames. The GIF to sprite sheet workflow reconstructs the full image for each moment, including transparent areas and frame disposal. Original frame timing stays available for animation preview and JSON export; you can override it with a consistent FPS when needed.

features.title: Combine images without stretching them
features.text: When you combine images into a sprite sheet, the largest source width and height define the grid cell. Smaller images keep their original dimensions. Bottom-center alignment helps characters share a ground line, while center and top-left alignment suit effects or interface assets. Transparent source margins stay intact unless you turn on Crop transparent edges.

features.title: Preview the animation before exporting
features.text: Switch between the full sheet and sprite sheet animation preview to inspect both layout and motion. Pause on a frame, step forward or backward, and compare timing. Pixelated display keeps small sprites crisp; preview zoom changes what you see, not the resolution of the exported PNG.

maker.useCasesTitle: From PNG to sprite sheet for real game workflows

useCases.title: Character movement and action loops
useCases.text: Group a short walk, jump, or attack sequence into a regular grid for your game prototype. Put the frames in playback order and check the contact point at the bottom of each cell. If a character still appears to jump vertically, inspect the transparent margins in the source frames; alignment cannot infer the location of the feet.

useCases.title: Effects, icons, and imported animation
useCases.text: Use horizontal strips for small effects, or a compact grid for icons and animation frames. GIF input is useful when the animation already exists as one file. This sprite sheet creator packages existing artwork; it does not invent in-between frames or turn a still image into a new animated character.

maker.guideTitle: Sprite sheet settings and export details

guide.title: Columns, margins, and frame spacing
guide.text: Columns control how many cells appear across a grid. Outer margin adds empty space around the sheet, while frame gap separates neighboring cells. These are different settings: importing the wrong gap into an engine can make the next sprite bleed into a frame. The displayed output dimensions update as you adjust the layout.

guide.title: Transparent PNG and JSON coordinates
guide.text: The default export background is transparent; a selected solid color is baked into the PNG. JSON uses a TexturePacker-style hash with unique filenames, source dimensions, frame rectangles, and duration. You can also export JSON Array, CSS, XML, or an animated GIF in the same ZIP. PNG grid slicing and JSON atlas import are different workflows; see the engine notes in the export panel.

guide.title: Practical browser limits
guide.text: Files are processed locally with no upload endpoint. The input limit is 50 MiB and 256 frames, with a 32-million-pixel decoded frame budget. Each source image or output sheet is limited to 8192 pixels per edge and 16 million pixels. Reduce dimensions or split a long animation if a limit is reached. Refreshing the page clears the workspace.

maker.faqText: Practical details about exporting sheets, GIF timing, and what this free tool does not do.

faq.title: Is this online sprite sheet maker really free?
faq.text: Yes. Combining images, extracting GIF frames, previewing, and downloading the result are free and do not require registration. AI asset generation is a separate product flow; it is not a step you must complete to get your exported sheet.

faq.title: Can I create a transparent sprite sheet from JPG?
faq.text: The unused space between JPG frames can be transparent, but a JPG has no alpha channel. Existing background pixels stay in the image. Use PNG or static WebP with transparency when you need a transparent character silhouette.

faq.title: Will a GIF keep its original animation speed?
faq.text: Yes, with Use frame timing enabled. Disable that option to apply one FPS value to every frame. A PNG cannot carry playback timing by itself; use the duration values in the JSON or configure timing in your engine.

faq.title: Can I cut the result and rearrange it again?
faq.text: Yes. Open in Cutter carries your sheet into the companion tool without a download and upload round trip. The handoff lasts within the current tab and does not survive a page refresh.

faq.title: Does this replace an advanced texture packer?
faq.text: This tool focuses on regular grids and strips. It can crop transparent margins when you enable that option. It does not rotate sprites, create polygon packing, or generate multiple atlas pages. Those specialized packing tasks require a different workflow.

maker.ctaTitle: Ready to make your sprite sheet?
maker.ctaText: Drop images or a GIF into the workspace above, arrange the frames, and export a PNG sheet. Files stay in this tab until you refresh.

splitter.title: Free Sprite Sheet Cutter
splitter.intro: Cut a sprite sheet into individual images with a grid you can actually inspect. This free sprite sheet cutter lets you adjust frame dimensions, offsets, and gaps, preview a selected animation, and download PNG frames as a ZIP — directly in your browser.
splitter.stepsTitle: How to cut a sprite sheet in three steps

steps.title: 1. Load your sprite sheet
steps.text: Upload one PNG, JPG, or static WebP image. The tool estimates a regular grid from its dimensions and slices it immediately; you can still adjust rows, columns, frame size, offsets, and gaps. If you still need a sheet, generate assets on the home page, then return here to cut your own artwork.

steps.title: 2. Match the grid to the frames
steps.text: Enter rows and columns if you know the layout, or switch to exact frame width and height. Set left and top offsets for an outer border, plus horizontal and vertical gaps between cells. Check the numbered overlay at a larger zoom so no frame crosses a cutting line.

steps.title: 3. Select, preview, and extract
steps.text: Select all frames, click individual cells, or enter a continuous range. Preview the selected animation to confirm the order, then download one PNG or a ZIP of frames. To rebuild a different grid or strip, download the frames and continue in Sprite Sheet Maker.

splitter.featuresTitle: A sprite sheet cutter that makes the boundaries visible

features.title: Slice by counts or exact dimensions
features.text: The sprite sheet cutter supports two ways to describe a regular grid. Rows and columns divide the usable image area into whole-pixel cells; frame dimensions use the exact width and height you enter. Switching modes carries valid computed values across, so you can refine a layout without starting the setup again.

features.title: Keep the frames you actually need
features.text: A single sheet may contain several actions and unused cells. Choose one range for a walk cycle, add specific frames with a click, or exclude cells whose pixels are entirely transparent. Original grid numbers remain visible even when your selection is smaller. Shift-click extends a selection from the last clicked frame.

features.title: Check motion before downloading files
features.text: Animation preview plays selected frames in row-major order: left to right, then top to bottom. Pause, step through the sequence, or set a uniform FPS to find an incorrect cut. When a sheet arrives from Maker, its frame names and timing accompany the original grid setup. A plain PNG upload has no timing metadata.

splitter.useCasesTitle: Cut frames from a sprite sheet for your next task

useCases.title: Separate a character action or effect
useCases.text: Extract a short idle, run, or attack loop from a larger animation sheet. The frame range controls make it easier to isolate one action while leaving the other rows alone. If the asset packs different actions in different rows, select the matching grid numbers instead of assuming that the entire sheet is one continuous animation.

useCases.title: Recover reusable PNG assets
useCases.text: Convert a sprite sheet to PNG files when you need individual icons, thumbnails, or frames for another editor. Each extracted image preserves the pixels inside its cell, including transparent padding. This sprite sheet cutter does not remove backgrounds, erase guide lines already baked into the source, or reinterpret the artwork.

splitter.guideTitle: Grid settings, edge checks, and PNG exports

guide.title: Offsets and gaps solve different problems
guide.text: An offset moves the first cutting cell away from the left or top image edge. A gap skips pixels between cells. Right and bottom margins can exclude an outer border, including margins passed from Maker. If every cut drifts farther from the artwork across a row, check the horizontal gap rather than shifting the entire grid.

guide.title: Understand unused edges and invalid grids
guide.text: Cells use whole pixels. When an image does not divide evenly, the tool reports unused pixels at the right and bottom instead of stretching the frames or silently treating a partial cell as complete. A grid that cannot fit a full frame blocks export. Recheck the dimensions against your source before accepting the preview.

guide.title: Download sprite frames as ZIP
guide.text: Select one frame for a direct PNG download or several for a ZIP containing consecutively numbered filenames. Grid numbers and source names help you trace each exported image back to its place in the sheet. Excluding transparent frames only removes fully transparent cells, not dark cells or images with a solid background.

guide.title: Local processing and memory limits
guide.text: Your image stays on your device. Uploads are limited to 50 MiB, 8192 pixels per edge, and 16 million pixels per source image. Extraction supports up to 256 frames and 32 million decoded frame pixels. Close an oversized selection or increase cell size if needed. The workspace is temporary, so download results before refreshing.

splitter.faqText: Practical details about automatic grid estimates, unused edges, downloads, and the limits of regular grids.

faq.title: How do I cut a sprite sheet into individual images?
faq.text: Upload the sheet, match its rows and columns or exact frame size, then select the cells to extract. Download produces one PNG for a single selected cell or a ZIP for several. The grid overlay shows the precise area used for each cut.

faq.title: Can this sprite sheet cutter detect irregular or tightly packed sprites?
faq.text: The tool estimates regular rectangular grids from image dimensions, but dimensions alone cannot reliably identify rotated frames, variable cell sizes, or tightly packed texture atlases. Those formats need frame metadata or a specialized unpacker. Adjust the estimate to the source specification when needed.

faq.title: Why do my extracted frames include another sprite?
faq.text: The cutting cells probably do not match the original frame dimensions or spacing. Zoom into the overlay and check the first cell, the next cell, and the final cell of a row. Correct offsets and gaps before exporting again.

faq.title: Can I turn a sprite sheet into a GIF?
faq.text: Yes. Check Include animated GIF before downloading a ZIP. The GIF plays the selected frames in order, using the current timing. PNG frames remain in the same archive.

faq.title: Do I need an account to use this free sprite sheet cutter?
faq.text: No account is required. You can cut a sprite sheet and download PNG frames or a ZIP without signing in. AI generation is optional and separate, available from the home page, and it never blocks your PNG or ZIP download.

splitter.relatedTitle: Build a new sheet from your selected frames
splitter.relatedText: Sprite Sheet Maker combines PNG frames or a GIF into a new grid or strip. After you download the extracted frames, you can change the arrangement, align different-sized images, or export a sheet with JSON coordinates.
